mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW X5 50e engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full BMW X5 50e engine replacement typically costs £4,500-£8,000 supply-only for a rebuilt B58B30S unit, or £6,500-£10,000 fitted by a specialist. Used engines start from £2,800, while reconditioned units typically cost £4,000-£6,000. Prices reflect the PHEV complexity - hybrid system recalibration is required. Professional fitting adds £800-£1,200 to any engine purchase. Rebuilt units include upgraded cooling and gasket components. 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty on all rebuilt engines.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the BMW X5 50e?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW X5 50e has three main areas of reported concern: drivetrain malfunction warnings (often software-related), hybrid cooling system issues, and high-voltage battery/charging system faults. Drivetrain warnings often resolved by software updates at dealer/specialist. Hybrid cooling system faults may require component replacement. Charging failures can be caused by firmware or 12V battery issues. The B58 combustion engine itself is robust and reliable. Drivetrain warnings should be investigated promptly - ignoring them can lead to more expensive repairs.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW X5 50e reliable? How long does the B58B30S engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B58 combustion engine in the X5 50e is based on BMW's proven B58 architecture, widely regarded as one of the most reliable modern petrol engines. However, the plug-in hybrid system introduces additional complexity. B58 engines regularly exceed 150,000-200,000 miles with proper maintenance. Hybrid system reliability is still emerging - early production has had some issues. Annual servicing (not just BMW's extended intervals) is critical. Many reported issues are software-related, not mechanical.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a BMW X5 50e?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2024-2025 X5 50e worth £73,000-£97,000, a £4,500-£8,000 rebuilt B58B30S engine represents excellent value - typically 5-10% of the vehicle's value. Replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value. If body, gearbox, and battery are sound, a rebuilt engine adds years of life. Used engine (£2,800-£4,500) is the budget option for short-term ownership. Rebuilt engine (£4,500-£8,000) offers warranty and peace of mind. Hybrid system complexity means specialist fitting is essential.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW X5 50e and the xDrive45e?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 50e (2024-present) replaced the 45e (2019-2024) as the flagship PHEV X5. The 50e offers significantly more power and electric range. 50e: 483-490hp, ~40 miles electric range. 45e: 394hp, ~29 miles electric range. 50e has a larger 25.7 kWh battery (up from ~17 kWh in the 45e). 50e features 7.4 kW AC charging (up from 3.7 kW). Engine codes are not interchangeable - always match the correct code.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my BMW X5 50e engine with a different size or fuel type?

acceptedAnswer.text: Engine swaps to a different size or fuel type are technically complex and rarely cost-effective on the G05 X5. Stick to like-for-like replacement using the correct B58B30S engine code for your X5 50e. ECU, wiring loom, fuel system, and exhaust all differ between petrol and diesel. Hybrid system components are engine-specific and require recalibration. High-voltage battery and electric motor are integrated with the engine system. Insurance must be notified of any non-standard engine swap. Specialist marketplace only recommends like-for-like code-matching for warranty coverage.

Powered by an uprated B58 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six petrol engine combined with a more powerful electric motor and a larger 25.7 kWh battery pack, the 50e delivers significantly more power and electric range than its predecessor.

commonProblems.h2: BMW X5 50e Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW X5 50e is powered by the B58B30S - a 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six petrol engine paired with a powerful electric motor integrated into the eight-speed automatic gearbox. While the B58 combustion engine is widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable modern powerplants, the plug-in hybrid system introduces additional complexity that can lead to expensive repairs. Rebuilt B58B30S engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Drivetrain Malfunction Warnings - Why the BMW X5 50e Displays Errors and Enters Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: The BMW X5 50e's complex hybrid system integrates the combustion engine, electric motor, high-voltage battery, and cooling systems. Early production examples have suffered from software-related drivetrain malfunction warnings, high-voltage system alerts, and cooling system issues. In some cases, the vehicle has become immobile due to drivetrain faults.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Dealer-level software update, system reset, and diagnostic check
repairOptions.longevity: 0-20,000 miles. Often resolves drivetrain warnings without hardware replacement.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty hybrid system components (cooling pump, sensors, wiring)
repairOptions.longevity: 20,000-60,000 miles. Required if software updates don't resolve persistent faults.

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - rebuilt/reconditioned engine + hybrid system
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt B58B30S engine with hybrid system recalibration, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if catastrophic combustion engine or hybrid system failure occurs.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2024-2025 BMW X5 50e is valued at approximately £73,000-£97,000 in the UK market. With a rebuilt B58B30S engine costing £4,500-£8,000 supply-only (plus £800-£1,200 fitting), replacement cost represents 5-10% of vehicle value - making full replacement financially viable even on the highest-mileage examples. However, the hybrid system complexity means specialist repair costs can escalate quickly.
problems.recommendation: The BMW X5 50e is a new model, and many reported issues are software-related rather than mechanical. If you experience drivetrain warnings, the first step should be a dealer-level software update and system reset - this resolves many early production issues. For persistent hybrid cooling system faults, specialist diagnosis is essential. Full engine replacement should only be considered if the combustion engine has suffered catastrophic failure - which is rare on the robust B58 platform. Always use a specialist with PHEV experience.

problems.group: High-Voltage Battery and Charging System Issues
problems.h4: High-Voltage Battery and Charging System Issues - Why the BMW X5 50e Won't Charge or Loses Range
problems.rootCause: The X5 50e's 25.7 kWh lithium-ion battery pack and 7.4 kW charging system are critical to the PHEV experience. Owners have reported charging failures following firmware updates, as well as 12V inverter supply line damage during assembly. Battery degradation can also reduce electric range over time.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Charging system diagnostic and firmware update
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic check, firmware update, charging system reset
repairOptions.longevity: 5,000-30,000 miles. First step for charging failures.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace 12V battery or repair inverter supply line
repairOptions.longevity: 10,000-40,000 miles. Required if 12V system failure is diagnosed.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty battery cells or entire high-voltage battery pack
repairOptions.longevity: 40,000+ miles. Only if battery degradation is severe.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See above. For a £73,000-£97,000 X5 50e, high-voltage battery repair or replacement represents 5-10% of vehicle value - significant but often justifiable given the vehicle's premium positioning.
problems.recommendation: If your X5 50e won't charge, start with a diagnostic check and firmware update - many charging issues are software-related. If the 12V battery fails, the vehicle may not recognise the key or start - this is a relatively inexpensive fix. High-voltage battery replacement is rare on low-mileage examples but should be considered if the vehicle is approaching 40,000+ miles with significant range loss. Always use a specialist with high-voltage system training.
